newsitem.title: PERU: Former U.N. chief charges Peru tapped his phone.
newsitem.headline: Former U.N. chief charges Peru tapped his phone.

text.p: Former United Nations chief Javier Perez de Cuellar said on Monday he would take the Peruvian government to court for tapping his telephones during the 1995 presidential campaign.
Perez de Cuellar alleges the National Intelligence Service listened in on his conversations during the campaign, which he lost to President Alberto Fujimori.
"Not only must this be investigated, it has to be punished as well. This is a criminal act," Perez de Cuellar, who heads Peru's main opposition party, Union for Peru, told reporters.

The former U.N. chief is the most high-profile target in a telephone espionage scandal that has damaged Fujimori's popularity. A local TV station alleged that security forces bugged the phones of up to 150 journalists and politicians.
"I hope the judge who deals with this case is not handpicked. We are tired of there being tapping (accusations) that just get filed away," Perez de Cuellar said.

Last month, cabinet ministers denied the wiretapping was connected to any organisation linked to the government. They claimed amateurs could have used simple electronic devices to listen in on conversations.
Although Perez de Cuellar said he had no proof, he said security forces must have been involved in the wiretapping.
"Some sector of the forces -- directly or indirectly -- has to be in charge of this widespread operation," he said.
Fujimori comfortably defeated Perez de Cuellar in the 1995 elections, gaining a second term with 65 percent of the vote.
Perez de Cuellar was U.N. secretary general from 1982 to 1991.
